text:
A 5-1 final reads like a rout, but the chances say otherwise. Over the full game, NYR created 3.68 expected goals to TBL's 2.59, and the simulated replays split almost evenly, 51 percent for TBL and 49 percent for NYR. TBL also had more shot attempts, 63 to 52. What separated the teams was Igor Shesterkin, who stopped 23 of 24 shots and saved 1.59 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved, while Andrei Vasilevskiy allowed 4 on 2.55 expected.

NYR built the lead early. Mika Zibanejad scored on a first-period power play at 5:34, with Pavel Dorofeyev and Adam Fox assisting. Dorofeyev made it 2-0 at 10:51 with a snap shot. TBL actually held the edge in that period, 1.06 expected goals to 0.58, but trailed anyway. Eeli Tolvanen then scored at 1:40 of the second on a 4 percent chance, a wrist shot that few models would have given a prayer.

Nikita Kucherov cut it to 3-1 at 7:59 of the second, also on a 4 percent chance, but NYR took over from there. They out-chanced TBL 1.60 to 0.84 in the second and 1.50 to 0.69 in the third. Gabe Perreault tipped in a fourth goal at 16:01 of the second, and Shesterkin closed the scoring himself at 17:26 of the third with a wrist shot, a 66 percent chance. TBL went 0 for 7 on the power play, with 0.45 expected goals from those chances.
